turns.text:
I'll explore the repo structure first to find the relevant files.The README already confirms `internal/mapengine/` is the map engine. Let me look at its structure and the engine-selection logic directly.Now let me get a structural map of these files plus find where engine selection/routing happens (likely a separate file, since routing wasn't in the tree listing — maybe it's in `internal/ghx` where `--map` is invoked).Found it — `types.go` has `Map`, `mapAuto`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback`, `normalizeEngine`. Let me read the key routing logic in full.Now let's check how the CLI wires `--map-engine` into this, and how `internal/ghx` invokes `mapengine.Map`.This confirms the full wiring, from CLI flag down to the engine dispatch. Let me pull the exact snippet in `read.go` to nail the call site.I have everything needed to answer precisely.

## Structural map engine — implementation

Package **`internal/mapengine`** (confirmed by ADR `docs/adr/0013-ghx-map-command.md`: *"`internal/mapengine` owns `Mapper`, `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`, engine selection, fallback, and output formatting"*).

Files (all in `internal/mapengine/`):
- **`types.go`** — shared types (`Engine`, `Level`, `Kind`, `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`, the `Mapper` interface) and the **top-level dispatcher**: `Map()`, `mapAuto()`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback()`, `NormalizeOptions()`/`normalizeEngine()`.
- **`goast.go`** — `GoASTMapper` (`Map` method), built on Go's standard `go/ast` + `go/token`; walks top-level `ast.FuncDecl`/`ast.GenDecl` nodes (`goASTSymbols`, `goFuncDeclSymbol`, `goTypeSymbol`, `receiverTypeName`).
- **`treesitter.go`** — `TreeSitterMapper` (`Map` method), wraps the external `gotreesitter` library (`odvcencio/gotreesitter`), with per-language `TreeSitterLanguageConfig` (tag queries, kind mapping, signature extraction, parent/method association via `computeTreeSitterParents`).
- **`regex.go`** — `RegexMapper` (`Map` method), a per-language table of regex rules (`regexRules`, `rulesForPath`) used as universal fallback.
- **`regex_test.go`** — engine-selection and fallback behavior tests (e.g. `TestMapAutoUsesGoASTForGoFiles`, `TestMapAutoUsesTreeSitterForTS/Python/Rust`, `TestTreeSitterEngineFallsBackToRegex`).

## Per-file engine selection

Selection happens in `mapengine.mapAuto()` (`internal/mapengine/types.go`), keyed on the file extension via `filepath.Ext(path)`:

```go
func mapAuto(path string, content []byte, opts Options) (Result, error) {
    switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path)) {
    case ".go":
        result, err := GoASTMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
        if err == nil { return result, nil }
        fallback, _ := RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
        fallback.Fallback = true
        return fallback, nil
    case ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".py", ".rs":
        return mapTreeSitterWithFallback(path, content, opts, false)
    default:
        return RegexMapper{}.Map(path, content, opts)
    }
}
```

Rules:
- **`.go`** → `GoASTMapper` (Go's own `go/ast`), falling back to `RegexMapper` on error.
- **`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js`/`.jsx`/`.py`/`.rs`** → `TreeSitterMapper` via `mapTreeSitterWithFallback`, which falls back to `RegexMapper` (setting `Fallback: true`) if tree-sitter errors, e.g. `ErrUnsupportedLanguage`.
- **everything else** → `RegexMapper` directly.

This dispatch only runs when `Options.Engine == EngineAuto` (the default via `normalizeEngine`, which maps anything not exactly `"regex"` or `"tree-sitter"` to `"auto"`). A caller can force an engine explicitly: `Map()` in the same file branches on `opts.Engine` — `EngineRegex` → `RegexMapper` directly, `EngineTreeSitter` → `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=true)`, `EngineAuto` → `mapAuto`.

**Wiring from the CLI**: `internal/cli/ghx.go` registers the `--map-engine` flag (default `"auto"`, line 211) on the `read` command, reads it into `mapEngine` (line 112), and passes it through as `ReadOpts.MapEngine` (line 120). `internal/ghx/read.go` (lines 186-191) is the call site that invokes `mapengine.Map(path, content, mapengine.Options{Engine: mapengine.Engine(opts.MapEngine), Level: ..., Kind: ...})` per file when `--map` is set — confirming ADR 0013's claim that `read.go` "calls `mapengine.Map(...)` and has no parser logic itself."

**Not verified**: I did not read the full bodies of `treesitter.go`'s tag-query configs or `regex.go`'s per-language rule tables line-by-line (only their structural maps), nor did I check `internal/mapengine/goast.go`'s multi-line-signature/generic-handling code in full — the map/grep output above covers signatures and the dispatch logic, which is what answers this question, but not every internal helper's implementation detail.

README:
# ghx — GitHub Code Exploration for AI Agents

One command does what takes 3-5 API calls. Batch file reads, code maps, search — all via `gh` CLI. Write JS programs that compose operations in one round-trip.

## Why

An agent wants to understand `packages/shadcn/src/utils/` in [shadcn-ui/ui](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui):

**With `gh` CLI** — 4 turns, 4 API calls, reads 3 full files (3,761 tokens), sees 3 of 34 files:
```
gh api /repos/shadcn-ui/ui/contents/packages/shadcn/src/utils       → JSON with shas, urls, links (480 tokens for a file list)
gh api /repos/.../get-config.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (1,981 tokens — agent only needed exports)
gh api /repos/.../registries.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (676 tokens)
gh api /repos/.../frameworks.ts --jq '.content' | base64 -d         → full file (624 tokens)
```

**With ghx** — 2 turns, 2 API calls, maps 10 files (3,058 tokens), sees signatures of all 10:
```
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui packages/shadcn/src/utils                     → directory listing (199 tokens)
ghx read shadcn-ui/ui "packages/shadcn/src/utils/*.ts" --map        → signatures of 10 files (2,859 tokens)
```

Same token budget. The `gh` agent read 3 full files. The ghx agent saw the structure of 10 — imports, exports, function signatures — and knows which ones to drill into. Pass a file, get content. Pass a directory, get a listing. Pass a glob, get matching files. Same command, always useful output.
